$description: Design tokens extracted from packages/design-system/src/css/{_palette.css,style.css,fonts.css}. This is the single source of truth used by the ComfyUI_frontend Tailwind 4 theme (@theme blocks). Always reference tokens by their Tailwind utility name (e.g. bg-secondary-background), never by raw hex value. Never use the `dark:` Tailwind variant — semantic tokens already resolve per-theme via the `.dark-theme` class selector.

color.$description: Two layers: `palette` (raw hue-ramp hex values, rarely referenced directly) and `semantic` (the tokens components and features actually use, resolved differently under `:root` (light) vs `.dark-theme`). Prefer semantic tokens. Use `bg-<name>`, `text-<name>`, `border-<name>` Tailwind utilities.

semantic.$description: Each entry resolves to a different palette color under :root (light) vs .dark-theme. Values below are the *resolved* colors per mode, for agents that need to reason about actual appearance; in code always use the Tailwind class, never the hex.

secondary-background.usage: default control fill (inputs, textareas, buttons' secondary variant)

tertiary-background.usage: elements one step above secondary (e.g. nested surfaces on a modal)

brand-yellow.usage: brand accent, same in both themes

brand-blue.usage: brand accent, same in both themes

dialog-surface.usage: scrollbar thumb color, legacy dialog chrome

text-primary.usage: legacy alias, prefer base-foreground in new code

text-secondary.usage: legacy alias, prefer muted-foreground in new code

rules: Never hardcode hex values in components — map to a semantic Tailwind token.
Never use the `dark:` Tailwind variant. Semantic tokens already flip per-theme via the `.dark-theme` class; components should reference only the semantic class name.
Figma color tiers map as: Base -> base-background, Secondary -> secondary-background, Tertiary -> tertiary-background.

Figma tokens suffixed `-hover`/`-selected` are prototype-only in Figma; on the frontend those states come from the dedicated `-hover`/`-selected` semantic tokens above, or Tailwind `hover:`/`data-[state=selected]` modifiers — never color-mix an arbitrary opacity unless no semantic hover token exists.

inter.usage: the only font family in the system; loaded as a variable font (weight 100-900) via fonts.css

fontSize.$description: Tailwind's default type scale applies (text-xs through text-9xl) plus two custom extra-small sizes for dense UI (node widgets, badges).

sm.size: 0.875rem (Tailwind default) — most common body/control text size

bold.usage: DialogTitle uses font-semibold; headings use font-bold

spacing.$description: No custom spacing scale override exists — components use Tailwind's default spacing scale (0.25rem increments: p-1, p-2, gap-4, etc.) directly. Common recurring values observed in real components below.

common.field-gap: gap-1 (label to control), gap-2 (control internals), gap-4 (between fields in a form)
common.card-padding: p-4 (compact rows/dialog body), p-6 (larger free-standing panels)

radii.$description: No custom radius scale override exists — Tailwind's default `rounded-*` scale is used directly, applied per-component by convention rather than a strict system.

lg.usage: Input, Textarea, Dialog, Popover, compact card/list-row surfaces (rounded-lg border border-border-default p-4)

2xl.usage: large free-standing panels (rounded-2xl border border-border-default bg-base-background)

inset-highlight.value: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgb(from white r g b / 0.1)

zIndex.$description: No formal token scale — the codebase uses one recurring bare value for all floating/portaled UI so overlays consistently stack above app chrome.

modal-and-overlay.usage: Dialog overlay/content, Popover content, HoverCard content, AccessibleTooltip content, ui/Popover.vue menu content. When a component must render above a PrimeVue-managed dialog whose z-index is dynamic, use the `useModalLiftedZIndex` composable instead of a static class.

iconography.$description: Two icon systems, both Iconify-driven Tailwind utilities — never inline SVG or an icon font.

lucide.usage: general UI icons (chevrons, x, search, plus/minus, etc.)
lucide.sizing: use `size-*` utilities, e.g. size-4; unsized svgs inside Button auto-size to size-4

comfy.usage: brand/provider/node-category glyphs, source SVGs in packages/design-system/src/icons/
comfy.sizing: same as lucide — size-*, never font-size

iconography.rule: NEVER size icon-[...] utilities with text-* font-size classes — Iconify icons scale via width/height (1.2em), so font-size produces unpredictable results.

sizes.$description: No custom icon-size scale override exists — Tailwind's default `size-*` scale is used directly, same pattern as spacing above.
sizes.size-4: 16px — default; by far the most common icon size in production
sizes.size-8 / size-10 / size-12: 32–48px — illustrative/decorative only (empty states, upload/preview placeholders), not general UI chrome

commonIcons.$description: Real icon names pulled from production usage, ranked by occurrence count in src/ as of this skill's creation. Not exhaustive — use as a starting vocabulary, then verify any specific name still resolves against packages/design-system/src/icons/ (comfy) or iconify's lucide set before shipping.
commonIcons.$regenerate: grep -rohoE "icon-\[lucide--[a-zA-Z0-9-]+\]" src --include=*.vue --include=*.ts | sed -E 's/icon-\[lucide--([a-zA-Z0-9-]+)\]/\1/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn   (swap the pattern for icon-(mask-)?\[comfy--...\] to get the comfy list)

comfy.$note: Provider/brand names (gemini, bytedance, tencent, kling, grok, bfl, openai, ...) are third-party logos, not general-purpose icons — only use them to label that specific provider's content, never decoratively.
